definition_zh: 辐射；放射线；辐射能；放射治疗
definition_en: energy travelling outward from a source as waves or particles, and the process by which such energy spreads
core_image: 一盏灯从中心向四周射出一圈圈同心波纹，越远越淡
scene: Thick lead shielding keeps radiation from reaching the laboratory workers.
sceneCN: 这里 radiation 指「电离辐射」（第 4 个义项：能量足以使原子电离的射线）；铅屏蔽把射线挡住，保护实验人员。图中可辨识物件：铅砖、辐射警示标志、同心波纹、盖革计数器。

pos.zh: 辐射；放射线；辐射能；放射治疗（指能量时多不可数，指多种射线时可用复数 radiations）

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: radiation（指能量整体时通常不加 -s）

derivatives.zh: 光芒四射的；容光焕发的

senses.title: Energy sent out from a source
senses.titleCN: 放射：能量自源头向四周送出
senses.definition: energy that travels outward from a source in the form of waves or moving particles
senses.definitionCN: 以波或运动粒子的形式从源头向外传播的能量
senses.example: A heater warms a room mainly by radiation and convection.
senses.exampleCN: 取暖器主要靠辐射和对流让房间变暖。
senses.why: Latin radius first named a wheel spoke and later a ray of light; radiatio named the act of sending out rays, so the noun begins with the picture of spokes leaving a centre.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 radius 最初指车轮辐条，后指光线；radiatio 指射出光线的动作，因此这个名词的起点是辐条自中心向外伸出的画面。

senses.title: Heat transfer without contact
senses.titleCN: 辐射传热：不靠物质接触传热
senses.definition: the mode of heat transfer in which energy moves as electromagnetic waves, with no material carrying it
senses.definitionCN: 热量以电磁波传递、无需任何材料携带的传热方式
senses.example: A vacuum flask slows heat loss because radiation is the only route left.
senses.exampleCN: 真空瓶能减缓散热，因为剩下的传热途径只有辐射。
senses.why: Physics kept the outward-ray image for the third mode of heat transfer, beside conduction and convection.
senses.whyCN: 物理学沿用了「向外射出的光线」这一意象，把它当作传导、对流之外的第三种传热方式。

senses.title: The electromagnetic spectrum
senses.titleCN: 电磁辐射：从无线电波到伽马射线的谱段
senses.definition: electromagnetic radiation taken as a whole family, from radio waves through visible light to gamma rays
senses.definitionCN: 作为一整类看待的电磁辐射，涵盖无线电波、可见光直至伽马射线
senses.example: Sunlight is electromagnetic radiation with its peak in the visible band.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光是电磁辐射，其峰值位于可见光波段。
senses.why: All of these waves are emitted by accelerating charges, so one noun covers the whole spectrum.
senses.whyCN: 这些波都由加速运动的电荷发出，因此一个名词就覆盖了整个谱段。

senses.title: Ionizing radiation
senses.titleCN: 电离辐射：能量高到能击出电子
senses.definition: radiation energetic enough to strip electrons from atoms, including alpha, beta, gamma and X-rays
senses.definitionCN: 能量足以使原子失去电子的辐射，包括 α 射线、β 射线、γ 射线与 X 射线
senses.example: Ionizing radiation can damage DNA, and high doses raise cancer risk.
senses.exampleCN: 电离辐射会损伤 DNA，高剂量会提高癌症风险。
senses.why: Twentieth-century physics added the word ionizing when the defining effect became the removal of electrons from matter.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪物理学加上 ionizing 一词，因为其决定性效应变成了从物质中剥离电子。

senses.title: Radiotherapy
senses.titleCN: 放射治疗：用射线摧毁病灶
senses.definition: in medicine, the controlled use of ionizing radiation to destroy tumour cells
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指受控地使用电离辐射来杀灭肿瘤细胞
senses.example: She had six weeks of radiation after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她接受了六周放射治疗。
senses.why: Therapy applies the physical emission to a clinical target, and everyday usage shortened the phrase radiation therapy to radiation.
senses.whyCN: 治疗把物理上的放射用于临床靶区，日常用法又把 radiation therapy 简称为 radiation。

senses.title: Spreading out from a centre
senses.titleCN: 辐射状扩散：自中心向四周铺开
senses.definition: a pattern in which something spreads outward from one point, the way spokes or ripples do
senses.definitionCN: 事物自一点向四周铺开的格局，如同辐条或水波那样
senses.example: The radiation of suburbs from the old core reshaped the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 郊区自老城核心向外辐射扩散，重塑了整个区域。
senses.why: The spoke image returns here: anything arranged like spokes around a hub can be said to radiate.
senses.whyCN: 辐条意象在此回归：凡是像辐条一样围绕轴心排布的事物，都可以说在辐射。

senses.title: Adaptive radiation
senses.titleCN: 适应辐射：一个谱系分化出众多物种
senses.definition: in evolutionary biology, the rapid splitting of one ancestral lineage into many forms that fill different niches
senses.definitionCN: 进化生物学中指一个祖先谱系迅速分化成许多占据不同生态位的形态
senses.example: Darwin's finches are a classic case of adaptive radiation on islands.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文雀是岛屿上适应辐射的经典案例。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the image of branches spreading from one point: a single stock radiates into many species.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用了「自一点向四周分枝」的意象：一个类群辐射成许多物种。

senses.title: Antenna radiation pattern
senses.titleCN: 天线辐射图：发射功率在空间中的分布
senses.definition: in radio engineering, the spatial distribution of the power an antenna emits
senses.definitionCN: 无线电工程中，天线所发射功率在空间里的分布形态
senses.example: The antenna's radiation pattern is strongest along the horizontal plane.
senses.exampleCN: 该天线的辐射图在水平面上最强。
senses.why: Engineering asks where the emitted waves actually go, so here radiation names outgoing power rather than a harmful ray.
senses.whyCN: 工程学关心发射波的实际去向，因此这里的 radiation 指向外发出的功率，而不是有害射线。

intro.en: Radiation comes from the Latin noun radiatio, built on the verb radiare 'to emit rays', which in turn rests on radius 'spoke, ray'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: radiation 出自拉丁名词 radiatio，它由动词 radiare「发出光线」构成，而 radiare 又基于 radius「辐条、光线」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin radius named the spoke of a wheel and also a ray or beam of light. The spoke sense is the older one; how the ray sense grew out of it is generally explained by the straight line running from a hub outward, but the exact path is not recorded.
items.cn: 拉丁 radius 指车轮辐条，也指光线或光束。辐条义更早；光线义如何由它引申，通常用「自轴心向外延伸的直线」来解释，但确切路径并无记录。

items.en: The verb radiare meant 'to furnish with rays, to shine', and the action noun radiatio meant 'a shining, a radiation'. Both are recorded in classical and later Latin.
items.cn: 动词 radiare 意为「使带光线、发光」，动作名词 radiatio 意为「发光、放射」。两者在古典拉丁及后世拉丁文中均有记录。

items.en: English radiation appears in the sixteenth century with the general sense 'the act of radiating or spreading out'. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 radiation 于 16 世纪出现，泛指「放射或向外扩散的动作」。最早的确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics gave the word its technical centre: energy carried by electromagnetic waves. The older sense of spreading outward was simply narrowed to a physical mechanism.
items.cn: 19 世纪物理学赋予该词技术核心：由电磁波携带的能量。原先「向外扩散」的旧义被收窄为一种物理机制。

items.en: In the twentieth century radiation also came to name alpha, beta and gamma rays from unstable nuclei, and by extension radiation therapy in hospitals.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，radiation 又用于指不稳定原子核发出的 α、β、γ 射线，并引申出医院的放射治疗。

items.en: The first English date is uncertain, and the deeper origin of Latin radius before its 'spoke' sense is not established; any Indo-European form behind it would be a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：英语首见年代存疑；拉丁 radius 在「辐条」义之前的更深来源并无定论，其背后的任何印欧形式都属重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms that stress emission or the emitted material.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是强调发射行为或发射物的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb for sending out rays or showing a quality; it names the act, while radiation names the energy or the process as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指发出射线或显露某种气质；它表示动作，而 radiation 把能量或过程当作事物来命名。

entries.definition: Means 'sending out light' or 'showing great happiness'. It describes a source or a face, not the energy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「发光的」或「容光焕发的」，描述发光体或面容，而不是能量本身。

entries.definition: The physical device that gives off heat, especially in a car or a room. It is a countable object and never the heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指放出热量的实体装置，尤指汽车或房间里的散热器；是可数物件，绝不指热量。

entries.definition: The act of subjecting something to radiation. Radiation goes out from a source; irradiation is what the target receives.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物接受辐射的处理。radiation 是源头向外发出，irradiation 是目标物受到照射。

entries.definition: A general word for anything sent out, including gases and sound; radiation is one special case, tied to waves or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何被送出的东西，包括气体与声音；radiation 是其中与波或粒子相关的特例。

entries.definition: The property of unstable nuclei emitting radiation. It names the capacity, while radiation names what is actually emitted.
entries.definitionCN: 指不稳定原子核发射辐射的性质；它命名的是能力，radiation 命名的是实际发出的东西。

entries.definition: A narrow, directed stream of particles or light. Radiation can spread in all directions; a beam is deliberately confined.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄而有方向的粒子流或光束。radiation 可以向四面八方扩散，beam 则被有意约束成束。

entries.definition: Radioactive material that settles after an explosion or accident. It is the contaminated dust, not the rays in flight.
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸或事故后沉降下来的放射性物质；指受污染的尘埃，而不是飞行中的射线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: radius 'spoke' + -ation: rays leaving a hub like spokes.
normal.cn: radius「辐条」+ -ation：光线像辐条一样自轴心射出。

normal.en: The family runs radiate, radiator, radiant, radial, radioactive and radiotherapy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 radiate、radiator、radiant、radial、radioactive、radiotherapy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: ionizing radiation, electromagnetic radiation, radiation therapy, background radiation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义项：电离辐射、电磁辐射、放射治疗、本底辐射。

normal.en: Physics counts three modes of heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation.
normal.cn: 物理学把传热分为三种方式：传导、对流、辐射。

normal.en: irradiation is the target's side of the event; radiation is the source's side.
normal.cn: irradiation 是目标物承受的一面，radiation 是源头发出的一面。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water: rings run outward from one point and weaken with distance.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落入静水：圆环自一点向外跑，越远越弱。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel whose spokes are drawn as thin lines of light leaving the hub.
abstract.cn: 想象一个车轮，辐条被画成离开轴心的细光线。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where one lamp makes every wall equally lit, with no material flowing between lamp and wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗室，一盏灯把每面墙都照亮，而灯与墙之间没有任何物质流动。

examples.en: Background radiation from rocks and cosmic rays is present everywhere.
examples.cn: 来自岩石与宇宙射线的本底辐射无处不在。

examples.en: The doctor lowered the radiation dose to protect the patient's healthy tissue.
examples.cn: 医生降低了辐射剂量，以保护患者的健康组织。

examples.en: Adaptive radiation filled the young lake with dozens of related fish species.
examples.cn: 适应辐射让这个年轻的湖泊里出现了数十种近缘鱼类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「射线（radio）自中心四散」——由一点向四周发出能量 → radiation 辐射、放射线

root: 拉丁 radius「辐条、光线」→ radiare「发光、放射」→ radiatio「放射」；英语 radiation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: spokes of energy leave a centre, and that leaving is read as heat, as light, as danger, as therapy, or as a pattern of spread.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：能量的「辐条」离开发射中心，而这一次离开可被读成热、读成光、读成危险、读成治疗，也可读成一种扩散格局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: spokes of energy leaving a hub and thinning with distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：能量的辐条离开轴心，越远越稀薄。

branches.en: PLAIN EMISSION: energy leaves a source, whether as a general process or as the third mode of heat transfer.
branches.cn: 单纯发射：能量离开源头，或作为一般过程，或作为第三种传热方式。

branches.en: THE WHOLE SPECTRUM: radio, light and gamma rays are one family because one mechanism emits them.
branches.cn: 整个谱段：无线电波、光与伽马射线同属一族，因为由同一种机制发出。

branches.en: HIGH ENERGY: when the rays can strip electrons, radiation becomes a hazard and also a medical tool.
branches.cn: 高能一端：当射线能够剥离电子，辐射既成为危害，也成为医疗工具。

branches.en: SPATIAL PATTERN: the spoke image returns for things spreading from a centre, including antenna power.
branches.cn: 空间格局：辐条意象回归，用于自中心扩散的事物，包括天线功率分布。

branches.en: EVOLUTIONARY BRANCHING: one ancestral stock radiates into many species, borrowing the same outward picture.
branches.cn: 进化分枝：一个祖先类群辐射成许多物种，借用的仍是同一幅向外铺开的图。

intro.en: Radiation is a Latin noun of action laid onto an English noun ending: a root for 'spoke, ray', a verb of emitting, and the suffix -ation.
intro.cn: radiation 是拉丁动作名词加上英语名词词尾的构造：一个表示「辐条、光线」的词根，一个表示发射的动词，以及后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius 'spoke, ray' supplies radius, radiate, radiant, radial, radiator and radiation; the same root also underlies radio, though that word was shortened from radiotelegraphy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 radius「辐条、光线」衍生了 radius、radiate、radiant、radial、radiator、radiation；同一词根也支撑 radio，但 radio 是 radiotelegraphy 的缩略。

items.meaning: a sending out of rays; the energy so sent
items.meaningCN: 射出光线的动作；如此射出的能量
items.example: Radiation from the sample was measured for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 对样品的辐射测量了一个小时。

items.meaning: to send out rays or spread from a centre
items.example: Warmth radiated from the stones after sunset.
items.exampleCN: 日落之后，石头仍在散发热量。

items.meaning: a device that gives off heat
items.example: The radiator clicked as the room cooled.
items.exampleCN: 房间变冷时，散热器发出咔哒声。

items.meaningCN: 向外发光的；容光焕发的
items.example: The bride looked radiant in the doorway.
items.exampleCN: 新娘站在门口，容光焕发。

items.meaning: arranged along rays from a centre
items.meaningCN: 沿自中心发出的射线排列的
items.example: The tyre has a radial steel belt.
items.exampleCN: 这种轮胎带有径向钢丝带。

items.meaningCN: 原子核不稳定而发出电离射线
items.example: The sample was too radioactive to handle.
items.exampleCN: 该样本放射性太强，无法直接操作。

items.example: Radiotherapy followed the surgery.
items.exampleCN: 手术之后进行了放射治疗。

items.example: The seeds were irradiated to kill insects.
items.exampleCN: 种子经辐照处理以杀灭害虫。

latinEntries.meaning: spoke of a wheel; ray of light
a shining; a sending out of rays

definition_zh: 放射性的；具放射性的；受放射性污染的
definition_en: emitting ionizing radiation because atomic nuclei are unstable, or relating to such emission
core_image: 一块泛着幽绿光的矿石旁边，盖革计数器的指针猛然跳起
scene: Uranium ore is radioactive, so it must be handled behind thick shielding.
sceneCN: 这里 radioactive 指「具放射性的」（第 1 个义项：原子核不稳定而自发发出电离辐射）；因此铀矿石必须在厚屏蔽后处理。图中可辨识物件：铀矿石、盖革计数器、辐射标志、铅手套。

pos.zh: 放射性的；具放射性的；与放射性有关的；受放射性污染的
放射性物质（多见于 radioactive(s) 的旧式说法）

senses.title: Emitting ionizing radiation
senses.titleCN: 具放射性的：原子核不稳定自发发出射线
senses.definition: giving off ionizing radiation because the atomic nuclei are unstable
senses.definitionCN: 因原子核不稳定而发出电离辐射
senses.example: Uranium ore is radioactive and sets off a Geiger counter.
senses.exampleCN: 铀矿石具有放射性，会让盖革计数器响起。
senses.why: The adjective joins radio- 'ray' to active 'doing': the material is actively giving out rays rather than merely reflecting them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把表示「射线」的 radio- 与表示「起作用的」active 结合起来：材料在主动发出射线，而不只是反射射线。

senses.title: Relating to the phenomenon
senses.titleCN: 放射性现象的：用作技术修饰语
senses.definition: used in technical phrases to name the process or property of emitting rays
senses.definitionCN: 在技术短语中命名发射射线的过程或性质
senses.example: Radioactive decay follows a fixed half-life for each isotope.
senses.exampleCN: 每种同位素的放射性衰变都遵循固定的半衰期。
senses.why: Once the noun radioactivity was coined, the adjective became the general label for anything belonging to that phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: radioactivity 这一名词出现后，形容词便成为指属该现象的一般标签。

senses.title: Contaminated by radioactive material
senses.titleCN: 受放射性污染的：沾上了放射性物质
senses.definition: made dangerous by contact with radioactive material rather than by its own nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 因接触放射性物质而变得危险，而不是自身原子核不稳定
senses.example: The scrap yard was declared radioactive after the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后，这家废料场被宣布受到放射性污染。
senses.why: Contamination spreads the label from the source to whatever the material touches, so objects can be radioactive without being radioactive substances.
senses.whyCN: 污染把这个标签从源头传播到材料接触过的一切，因此物品可以「受放射性污染」而本身并不是放射性物质。

senses.title: Of an unstable isotope
senses.titleCN: 放射性同位素的：指不稳定核素
senses.definition: describing an isotope whose nuclei decay spontaneously, often used before isotope or element names
senses.definitionCN: 形容原子核自发衰变的同位素，常用于 isotope 或元素名称之前
senses.example: Carbon-14 is the radioactive isotope used to date organic remains.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-14 是用来给有机遗存定年的放射性同位素。
senses.why: Chemistry distinguishes stable from unstable isotopes with this adjective, keeping the physical meaning close to the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 化学用这个形容词区分稳定与不稳定同位素，其物理含义紧贴第一义项。

senses.title: Used for dating
senses.titleCN: 用于定年：靠衰变速度推算年代
senses.definition: in geology and archaeology, describing a method that measures the decay of isotopes to estimate age
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学与考古学中，形容通过测量同位素衰变来估算年代的方法
senses.example: Radioactive dating placed the rock at about 2.5 billion years.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性定年把这层岩石测定在约 25 亿年前。
senses.why: Because decay runs at a steady rate, a radioactive clock can be read long after the event, and the adjective names that clock.
senses.whyCN: 由于衰变速率稳定，放射性时钟在事件发生很久之后仍可读数，形容词命名的正是这只钟。

senses.title: Associated with nuclear waste
senses.titleCN: 与核废料相关的：长期危险的工业产物
senses.definition: describing waste from reactors or weapons programmes that stays hazardous for a very long time
senses.definitionCN: 形容反应堆或核武器计划产生的、长期保持危险的废物
senses.example: Radioactive waste must be stored deep underground for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性废物必须深埋地下，存放数千年。
senses.why: The nuclear industry extended the adjective to its by-products, where the danger lasts far longer than any human schedule.
senses.whyCN: 核工业把这个形容词扩展到其副产品，那里的危险远超任何人类时间表。

senses.title: Used as a tracer
senses.titleCN: 作示踪剂用的：让射线替人「看见」路径
senses.definition: describing a small amount of radioactive material used to follow movement through a body, pipe or plant
senses.definitionCN: 形容少量用于追踪物质在人体、管道或植物中运动的放射性材料
senses.example: A radioactive tracer showed where the fluid leaked from the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性示踪剂显示出液体从管道何处泄漏。
senses.why: The emitted rays act as a signal, so a tiny amount of radioactive substance can reveal a path without being seen directly.
senses.whyCN: 发出的射线充当信号，因此极少量放射性物质无需直接可见也能暴露路径。

senses.title: Figuratively explosive
senses.titleCN: 比喻上「带辐射」的：碰不得的敏感议题
senses.definition: in informal speech, describing a topic or person so controversial that others avoid touching it
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某话题或人物争议极大，别人都避而远之
senses.example: The old lawsuit became politically radioactive during the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩旧诉讼在竞选期间变成了政治上碰不得的议题。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the idea of invisible danger: as with real radioactivity, harm may follow mere contact, so people keep their distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了「看不见的危险」：如同真实放射性，仅仅接触就可能受害，于是人们保持距离。

intro.en: Radioactive is a modern compound of radio- 'ray' and active, coined at the end of the nineteenth century when rays from uranium were first studied. Elements of the history remain uncertain.
intro.cn: radioactive 是 radio-「射线」与 active 的现代复合词，在 19 世纪末人们开始研究铀射线时被造出。其历史细节仍有存疑处。

items.en: The combining form radio- goes back to Latin radius 'spoke, ray'. It entered modern science through words for rays and radiant energy.
items.cn: 构词成分 radio- 可追溯到拉丁 radius「辐条、光线」，经由指射线与辐射能的科学词汇进入现代用语。

items.en: Active comes from Latin activus, built on agere 'to do, drive'. The pair radio- + active literally suggests 'actively ray-emitting'.
items.cn: active 出自拉丁 activus，基于 agere「做、驱动」。radio- 与 active 的组合字面上就是「主动发出射线的」。

items.en: The compound radio-active is generally attributed to Marie Curie's circle in 1898, in the period when polonium and radium were being isolated. The precise first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合词 radio-active 一般认为出自 1898 年前后居里夫妇的圈子，正值分离钋与镭的时期。最早的印刷使用确切出处存疑。

items.en: English quickly adopted radioactive for any substance giving off such rays, and radioactivity was formed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语很快用 radioactive 指任何发出这类射线的物质，并构成名词 radioactivity。

items.en: During the twentieth century the word spread from physics to medicine, industry, waste management and dating methods.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词从物理学扩展到医学、工业、废物管理与定年方法。

items.en: Attribution of the coinage is generally accepted rather than documented in every detail, and the exact first English citation remains uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（创造归属与首见书证）：该词的创造归属属于「一般认为是」，并非每个细节都有文献可证；英语最早书证也仍存疑。

note.en: The first group separates adjectives and nouns of the same ray-family; the second gives near-synonyms for danger or instability.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「射线词族」中的形容词与名词；第二组给出表示危险或不稳定的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to radiation as a mode of energy transfer, especially heat. It says nothing about unstable nuclei or contamination.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为能量传递方式（尤指传热）的辐射，与原子核不稳定或污染无关。

entries.definition: The energy or rays themselves. Radioactive describes the source; radiation is what leaves it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能量或射线本身。radioactive 描述源头，radiation 指离开源头的东西。

entries.definition: The property or process of emitting rays. It cannot stand before a noun the way radioactive can.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出射线的性质或过程，不能像 radioactive 那样直接放在名词前。

entries.definition: The everyday word for broadcast communication or its equipment, shortened from radiotelegraphy; not a synonym for radioactive.
entries.definitionCN: 指广播通信或其设备的日常词，由 radiotelegraphy 缩略而来，并非 radioactive 的同义词。

entries.definition: In nuclear slang, 'hot' means radioactive or highly contaminated. It is informal and depends on context.
entries.definitionCN: 在核工业俚语中，hot 指具放射性或污染严重的；属口语用法，且依赖语境。

entries.definition: Describing a nucleus that may decay. Unstable states the cause; radioactive states the observable emission.
entries.definitionCN: 形容可能衰变的原子核。unstable 说的是原因，radioactive 说的是可观测的发射现象。

entries.definition: Made impure by contact with a harmful substance. It can be chemical or radioactive, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 因接触有害物质而变得不纯；可以指化学污染，也可指放射性污染，范围更宽。

entries.definition: Relating to atomic nuclei or nuclear energy. A nuclear plant may handle radioactive material, but nuclear itself does not mean 'emitting rays'.
entries.definitionCN: 与原子核或核能有关。核电站会处理放射性物质，但 nuclear 本身不表示「发出射线」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: radio- 'ray' + active 'doing': the material is doing rays.
normal.cn: radio-「射线」+ active「起作用的」：材料在「做射线」。

normal.en: The family runs radioactivity, radiation, radioisotope, radionuclide, radiogenic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 radioactivity、radiation、radioisotope、radionuclide、radiogenic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: radioactive decay, radioactive waste, radioactive dating, radioactive tracer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：放射性衰变、放射性废物、放射性定年、放射性示踪剂。

normal.en: A Geiger counter clicks because the rays ionize gas inside it.
normal.cn: 盖革计数器会响，是因为射线电离了管内的气体。

normal.en: radiative is about heat transfer; radioactive is about unstable nuclei.
normal.cn: radiative 讲传热，radioactive 讲不稳定原子核。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that keeps warm by itself, never needing a fire, because the heat is made inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块不用火也一直温热的石头，因为热从它内部产生。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible drizzle falling from a rock, which only a clicking meter can hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一场自岩石落下的无形细雨，只有会咔哒响的仪表听得见。

abstract.en: Picture a warning sign painted on a box that no one dares to open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被画上警示标志，没人敢打开。

examples.en: Naturally radioactive rocks release radon gas into basements.
examples.cn: 天然放射性岩石会向地下室释放氡气。

examples.en: The laboratory stores radioactive waste in lead-lined containers.
examples.cn: 实验室把放射性废物存放在衬铅容器里。

examples.en: Investigators used a radioactive tracer to locate the underground leak.
examples.cn: 调查人员用放射性示踪剂定位地下泄漏点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「射线（radio）一直在动（active）」——不停向外发出射线 → radioactive 放射性的

root: 拉丁 radius「光线、辐条」+ activus「活动的」（agere「做」）；1898 年前后由 radio- 与 active 合成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the physical property to its uses: unstable nuclei emit rays, and that emission becomes a hazard, a clock, a tracer, a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从物理性质走向各种用途：不稳定核发出射线，而这一发射又变成危害、时钟、示踪剂与比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green-glowing ore making a meter needle jump.
core.cn: 核心意象：泛绿光的矿石让仪表指针猛跳。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: unstable nuclei emit ionizing rays, and the adjective names that process.
branches.cn: 性质本身：不稳定核发出电离射线，形容词命名这一过程。

branches.en: SPREAD BY CONTACT: the label moves from the source to whatever touches it.
branches.cn: 接触传播：标签从源头转移到它接触过的一切。

branches.en: THE ISOTOPE: chemistry uses the adjective to separate stable from unstable nuclear species.
branches.cn: 同位素：化学用该形容词区分稳定与不稳定的核素。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: steady decay becomes a clock, and emitted rays become a tracer signal.
branches.cn: 工具化：稳定衰变成为时钟，发出的射线成为示踪信号。

branches.en: LONG DANGER: industrial waste keeps the physical hazard, while politics turns it into a metaphor.
branches.cn: 长期危险：工业废物保留物理危害，政治则把它变成比喻。

intro.en: Radioactive is a modern scientific compound: a Latin-derived combining form for rays, plus an adjective of action, with -ity forming its noun.
intro.cn: radioactive 是现代科学复合词：拉丁来源的「射线」构词成分，加上表示动作的形容词，再由 -ity 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The ray family includes radius, radiate, radiant, radiation, radiator and radio; the 'do' family includes act, action, agent, active and actor. Radioactive sits where the two families meet.
latinIntro.cn: 射线词族包括 radius、radiate、radiant、radiation、radiator、radio；「做」词族包括 act、action、agent、active、actor。radioactive 正处在这两个词族的交会处。

items.example: The isotope is radioactive for thousands of years.
items.exampleCN: 该同位素在数千年内保持放射性。

items.meaning: the property of emitting such rays
items.example: Radioactivity was discovered before its cause was understood.
items.exampleCN: 放射性的发现早于人们理解其成因。

items.meaning: the rays sent out, or the act of sending them
items.example: Radiation from the sample was measured hourly.
items.exampleCN: 每小时测量一次样品的辐射。

items.meaning: to send rays out from a centre
items.example: The metal radiated heat long after the fire died.
items.exampleCN: 火熄灭很久后，金属仍在散发热量。

items.example: The lab ordered a short-lived radioisotope.
items.exampleCN: 实验室订购了一种短寿命放射性同位素。

items.example: Radionuclides vary greatly in half-life.
items.exampleCN: 不同放射性核素的半衰期差别很大。

items.example: Radiogenic heat keeps the mantle slowly moving.
items.exampleCN: 放射性成因热使地幔缓慢流动。

items.example: The mail was irradiated as a precaution.
items.exampleCN: 邮件经过辐照作为预防措施。

definition_zh: 理性；合理性；合乎逻辑的程度；理性思考能力
definition_en: the quality of being guided by reason, or the extent to which something can be justified by logic
core_image: 一个人在天平两端放上证据与反证，让指针慢慢停在正中
scene: Bounded rationality admits that real decisions are limited by time and incomplete information.
sceneCN: 这里 rationality 指「理性（有限理性理论中的决策理性）」（第 4 个义项：受时间与信息限制的理性）；句意：有限理性承认真实决策受时间与不完整信息限制。图中可辨识物件：天平、证据卡片、时钟、档案夹。

pos.zh: 理性；合理性；合乎逻辑；理性思考能力（多作不可数，指多种类型时可用复数 rationalities）

forms.label: 相关名词
forms.form: rationalism（理性主义；注意与 rationality 不同）

derivatives.zh: 理性主义者；理性主义的

senses.title: The capacity to reason
senses.titleCN: 理性能力：凭推理而非冲动行事的能力
senses.definition: the human capacity to think, weigh evidence and draw conclusions rather than act on impulse
senses.definitionCN: 人进行思考、权衡证据并得出结论、而非凭冲动行事的能力
senses.example: Rationality is what lets a child learn that a taller glass can hold less water.
senses.exampleCN: 理性让人能学会：更高的杯子未必装得下更多水。
senses.why: The noun is built on Latin ratio 'reckoning, reason', so rationality names the faculty of doing what ratio does: counting, comparing and concluding.
senses.whyCN: 该名词基于拉丁 ratio「计算、理性」，因此 rationality 命名的是执行 ratio 所做之事的能力：计数、比较与下结论。

senses.title: Logical consistency
senses.titleCN: 逻辑一致性：前提能否支撑结论
senses.definition: the property of an argument or belief whose parts support one another without contradiction
senses.definitionCN: 论证或信念的各部分互相支撑、不自相矛盾的性质
senses.example: The rationality of the argument depends on whether its premises really support the conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证是否合理，取决于其前提是否真的支持结论。
senses.why: Here the word shifts from the thinker to the product: a set of statements can be called rational when its internal links hold.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从思考者转向思考产物：一组陈述只要内部联系站得住，就可称为合理。

senses.title: Economic rational choice
senses.titleCN: 经济理性：按偏好选择最优方案
senses.definition: in economics, the assumption that agents choose the option that best satisfies their preferences given available information
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中假定行为者在既有信息下选择最能满足其偏好的方案
senses.example: Rationality in economics does not require perfect foresight, only consistent preferences.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学中的理性并不要求完美预见，只要求偏好一致。
senses.why: Model-builders narrowed ratio to a calculable rule: compare options, assign values, pick the highest. The noun then names that rule-following.
senses.whyCN: 建模者把 ratio 收窄为可计算的规则：比较选项、赋值、取最高者。该名词于是命名这种按规则行事。

senses.title: Bounded rationality
senses.titleCN: 有限理性：受时间与信息限制的理性
senses.definition: the theory that real decision-makers are rational only within limits set by time, information and mental capacity
senses.definitionCN: 认为真实决策者只在时间、信息与心智能力所设的界限内保持理性的理论
senses.example: Bounded rationality explains why managers satisfice instead of searching for the best option.
senses.exampleCN: 有限理性解释了管理者为何满足于够用方案，而不去搜寻最优选项。
senses.why: The phrase adds a boundary to the noun: reason still operates, but not with unlimited resources, so the result is 'good enough' rather than optimal.
senses.whyCN: 该短语给名词加上边界：理性仍在运作，但资源并非无限，因此结果只是「够用」而非最优。

senses.title: Justification by reasons
senses.titleCN: 理由正当性：信念或行动能否给出理由
senses.definition: in philosophy, the property of a belief or action that can be defended with reasons others could examine
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上指信念或行动能够用他人可检验的理由来辩护的性质
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether rationality alone can justify a moral belief.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问单凭理性是否就能为道德信念提供正当性。
senses.why: Ratio also meant 'account' in the sense of a reckoning given to someone; rationality keeps that courtroom flavour of being answerable with reasons.
senses.whyCN: ratio 也有「向人交代的账目」之义；rationality 保留了这种「能用理由作答」的法庭气息。

senses.title: Formal and institutional rationality
senses.titleCN: 形式理性：制度按可计算规则运转
senses.definition: in social theory, especially Weber, the organization of action by calculable rules rather than tradition or personal whim
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论（尤其韦伯）中指按可计算规则、而非传统或个人任性来组织行动
senses.example: Weber saw formal rationality in bureaucracy, double-entry bookkeeping and the modern state.
senses.exampleCN: 韦伯在官僚制、复式记账与现代国家中看到了形式理性。
senses.why: Modern institutions extended ratio into rules and records; the noun then describes a system whose operations can be calculated in advance.
senses.whyCN: 现代制度把 ratio 扩展为规则与记录；该名词于是描述一种其运作可被预先计算的系统。

senses.title: Administrative overreach
senses.titleCN: 行政理性的反噬：规则僵化到违背目的
senses.definition: the quality of an organization that is highly rational in procedure but may lose sight of its purpose
senses.definitionCN: 组织在程序上高度理性、却可能偏离其目的的性质
senses.example: Critics warn that administrative rationality can produce rules that defeat their own aims.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者警告，行政理性可能造出违背自身目标的规则。
senses.why: This sense is rationality seen from outside: the machinery is consistent, yet the consistency itself becomes the problem.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项是从外部看理性：机器本身自洽，但自洽反而成了问题。

senses.title: Instrumental efficiency
senses.titleCN: 工具理性：只问手段是否高效
senses.definition: the kind of reason that asks how efficiently a goal can be reached, without judging whether the goal is worth reaching
senses.definitionCN: 只追问达成目标的手段是否高效、不评判目标本身是否值得追求的那种理性
senses.example: Instrumental rationality can build an efficient machine for a pointless task.
senses.exampleCN: 工具理性可以为一项无意义的任务造出高效的机器。
senses.why: The word separates means from ends: ratio calculates the shortest path, and the noun names that calculation when it is detached from value.
senses.whyCN: 该词把手段与目的分开：ratio 计算最短路径，名词命名的是这种与价值脱钩的计算。

intro.en: Rationality is a Latin-derived noun: ratio 'reckoning, reason' produced rationalis 'of reason', and Late Latin added -itas to make rationalitas. The English word appears in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: rationality 是拉丁来源的名词：ratio「计算、理性」构成 rationalis「理性的」，晚期拉丁再加 -itas 造成 rationalitas。英语形式于 16 世纪出现。

items.en: Latin ratio meant 'a reckoning, account, calculation' and, by extension, 'reason'. It comes from ratus, the past participle of reri 'to reckon, think'. The deeper origin of reri is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁 ratio 意为「计算、账目、核算」，并引申为「理性」。它出自 reri「计算、思考」的过去分词 ratus。reri 的更深来源存疑。

items.en: Adding -alis produced rationalis 'belonging to reason, reasonable', the adjective behind English rational.
items.cn: 加上 -alis 构成 rationalis「属于理性的、合理的」，即英语 rational 背后的形容词。

items.en: Late Latin rationalitas named the quality of being reasonable. The suffix -itas is the ancestor of English -ity, which turns adjectives into names of qualities.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 rationalitas 指「合理」这一性质。后缀 -itas 是英语 -ity 的前身，把形容词变成性质名词。

items.en: English rationality entered in the sixteenth century, first in theological and philosophical writing about reason and its limits.
items.cn: 英语 rationality 于 16 世纪进入，最早见于讨论理性及其限度的神学与哲学写作。

items.en: Economics, decision theory, sociology and law each narrowed the word: rational choice, bounded rationality, formal rationality and the rationality test.
items.cn: 经济学、决策理论、社会学与法学各自收窄了词义：理性选择、有限理性、形式理性与合理性审查。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and any Indo-European root behind Latin reri would be a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；拉丁 reri 背后的任何印欧词根都属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: The first group separates forms of the same ratio family; the second gives near-synonyms that stress logic, fairness or mental health.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一 ratio 词族的不同形式；第二组给出强调逻辑、公平或心智健全的近义词。

entries.definition: Meaning 'based on reason'. It describes a person or act, while rationality names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「基于理性的」，描述人或行为；rationality 则命名这种性质本身。

entries.definition: A noun for the underlying explanation or justification of something. It is not the quality of being rational.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事物背后的解释或理由，并非「理性的性质」。

entries.definition: The philosophical position that reason is the main source of knowledge. Rationality is the capacity; rationalism is a theory about it.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为理性是知识主要来源的哲学立场。rationality 是能力，rationalism 是关于该能力的理论。

entries.definition: To reorganize something on rational lines, or to invent a plausible excuse. Neither meaning is the noun rationality.
entries.definitionCN: 指按理性原则重组某物，或编造看似合理的借口；两者都不是名词 rationality。

entries.definition: The power of thinking, or a ground for a belief. Reason is broader and can be countable; rationality stresses consistency and justification.
entries.definitionCN: 指思维能力，或信念的依据。reason 范围更广且可数；rationality 更强调一致性与可辩护性。

entries.definition: The quality of being sensible and fair. It leans toward practical fairness, while rationality leans toward logical structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指通情达理与公平，偏向实践中的公允；rationality 偏向逻辑结构。

entries.definition: The system of valid inference, or the coherence of an argument. Logic is the tool; rationality is the broader disposition to use it.
entries.definitionCN: 指有效推理的规则体系，或论证的连贯性。logic 是工具，rationality 是更广的运用倾向。

entries.definition: A legal and medical word for a sound mind. It contrasts with illness, not with irrational argument.
entries.definitionCN: 法律与医学用语，指心智健全；它与疾病相对，而不是与不合逻辑的论证相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ratio 'reckoning' + -ality: the quality of being able to reckon rightly.
normal.cn: ratio「核算」+ -ality：能够正确核算的性质。

normal.en: The family runs rational, rationally, rationalism, rationalist, rationalize, rationale.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rational、rationally、rationalism、rationalist、rationalize、rationale。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the disciplines: bounded rationality, economic rationality, formal rationality, instrumental rationality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学科用法：有限理性、经济理性、形式理性、工具理性。

normal.en: rationality is the quality; rationalism is the doctrine; rationale is the stated reason.
normal.cn: rationality 是性质，rationalism 是学说，rationale 是给出的理由。

normal.en: A rational decision can still be wrong; rationality is about the process, not the outcome.
normal.cn: 理性的决定仍可能出错；rationality 讲的是过程，不是结果。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales that keeps tipping until each side holds the same weight of evidence.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平不断倾斜，直到两边承载的证据重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where every claim must be entered with its receipt.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，每一条主张都必须附上收据才能入账。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that computes the shortest route but never asks whether the destination matters.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只计算最短路线、却从不问目的地是否重要的机器。

examples.en: The study tested the rationality of consumers' choices under time pressure.
examples.cn: 该研究检验了消费者在时间压力下选择的合理性。

examples.en: Bounded rationality does not abandon reason; it places reason inside real constraints.
examples.cn: 有限理性并未放弃理性，而是把理性放进真实约束之中。

examples.en: A purely instrumental rationality may be efficient and still aim at the wrong end.
examples.cn: 纯粹的工具理性可以很高效，却仍可能指向错误的目的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ratio（比例）算得清」——凡事按比例、按账目核算 → rationality 理性、合理性

root: 拉丁 ratio「计算、账目、理性」→ rationalis「理性的」→ 晚期拉丁 rationalitas；英语 rationality。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one idea: ratio is reckoning, and rationality is the quality of being reckonable, defensible, or efficiently calculated — in a mind, an argument, an economy or an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念：ratio 是核算，rationality 则是可核算、可辩护或可高效计算的性质——它可落在心智、论证、经济或制度上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale held level by equal weights of evidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：两边证据等重而保持水平的天平。

branches.en: MIND AND ARGUMENT: the faculty of reckoning, and the consistency of what it produces.
branches.cn: 心智与论证：核算能力，以及其产物的前后一致。

branches.en: CALCULATED CHOICE: economics turns reckoning into preference-maximizing selection.
branches.cn: 计算性选择：经济学把核算变成偏好最大化选择。

branches.en: LIMITS: the same choice, bounded by time and incomplete information.
branches.cn: 限度：同一种选择，被时间与不完整信息所限。

branches.en: ACCOUNTABILITY: reasons must be given, whether to a philosopher or to an institution.
branches.cn: 可交代性：无论面对哲学家还是制度，都必须给出理由。

branches.en: MACHINERY: rules can become rigid, and calculation can detach from the worth of its goal.
branches.cn: 机械性：规则会僵化，计算也会与目标的价值脱钩。

intro.en: Rationality is an adjective turned into a quality noun: Latin ratio, the adjective suffix -alis, then the abstract suffix -itas, carried into English as -ity.
intro.cn: rationality 是形容词转为性质名词：拉丁 ratio，加形容词后缀 -alis，再加抽象后缀 -itas，以英语 -ity 形式传入。

latinIntro.en: The ratio family includes ratio, rational, rationality, rationale, rationalize, ration and rate, all centred on counting and reckoning; ratio also gave the mathematical word ratio.
latinIntro.cn: ratio 词族包括 ratio、rational、rationality、rationale、rationalize、ration、rate，核心都在计数与核算；ratio 也直接成为数学里的「比」。

items.meaning: the quality of being guided by reason
items.example: The panel questioned the rationality of the pricing rule.
items.exampleCN: 专家组质疑该定价规则的合理性。

items.example: She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 她对延误给出了合理的解释。

items.example: He rationally weighed both offers.
items.exampleCN: 他理性地权衡了两份报价。

items.meaning: the view that reason is the chief source of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 认为理性是知识主要来源的学说
items.example: Rationalism contrasts with pure empiricism.
items.exampleCN: 理性主义与纯粹经验主义相对。

items.meaning: to organize on rational lines; to justify after the fact
items.meaningCN: 按理性重组；事后找理由
items.example: The firm rationalized its supply chain.
items.exampleCN: 该公司对供应链进行了合理化重组。

items.meaning: the stated set of reasons for something
items.meaningCN: 某事物明示的理由体系
items.example: The report explains the rationale for the new fee.
items.exampleCN: 报告解释了收取新费用的理由。

items.example: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.
items.exampleCN: 师生比是十比一。

items.meaning: the quality of being contrary to reason
items.example: The model allows for moments of irrationality.
items.exampleCN: 该模型容许非理性的时刻存在。

definition_zh: 理性地；合理地；合乎逻辑地；冷静地
definition_en: in a way that follows reason and evidence rather than impulse or emotion
core_image: 一个人把两张写满数据的纸并排铺开，逐行比对后才点头
scene: The committee rationally compared the costs before approving the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 rationally 是「以理性的方式」（第 1 个义项：依据推理与证据而非冲动）；句意：委员会在批准计划前理性地比较了各项成本。图中可辨识物件：数据表、双栏对比、铅笔、批准印章。

pos.zh: 理性地；合理地；合乎逻辑地；冷静地

collocations.zh: 与……有合理关联（法律用语）

senses.title: By reasoning
senses.titleCN: 凭推理地：按证据与逻辑推进
senses.definition: in a manner based on evidence and logical inference
senses.definitionCN: 以证据与逻辑推断为基础的方式
senses.example: She rationally compared the two offers before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在签字前理性地比较了两份报价。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to rational, so it names the manner of an act: the act is done the way ratio would do it, by counting and comparing.
senses.whyCN: 副词由 rational 加 -ly 构成，命名的是行为方式：该行为按 ratio 的方式来做，即计数与比较。

senses.title: Sensibly
senses.titleCN: 明智地：从实际后果出发
senses.definition: in a sensible way that takes likely consequences into account
senses.definitionCN: 以一种考虑可能后果的明智方式
senses.example: Rationally, the cheapest repair is to replace the whole unit.
senses.exampleCN: 从理性上看，最省钱的修法是整体更换。
senses.why: Reason applied to daily choices becomes prudence: the same adverb now means 'as common sense would advise'.
senses.whyCN: 把理性用于日常选择就变成审慎：同一个副词此时意为「按常识会建议的那样」。

senses.title: On economic grounds
senses.titleCN: 按经济核算地：依成本收益配置
senses.definition: in terms of cost and benefit, especially when allocating scarce resources
senses.definitionCN: 从成本与收益角度，尤其在配置稀缺资源时
senses.example: Resources are rationally allocated when prices reflect true scarcity.
senses.exampleCN: 当价格反映真实稀缺性时，资源才算被合理配置。
senses.why: Economics uses the adverb for decisions that maximize return under constraints, a narrowed form of reckoning.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用这个副词描述在约束下最大化收益的决策，是「核算」的收窄形式。

senses.title: Systematically
senses.titleCN: 系统地：按可重复的方法推进
senses.definition: in an orderly, methodical way that follows a procedure
senses.definitionCN: 以遵循程序的、有条理且可重复的方式
senses.example: The experiment was rationally designed, changing one variable at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 实验被合理地设计，每次只改变一个变量。
senses.why: Scientific method makes ratio procedural: steps are ordered so that results can be checked, and rationally marks that order.
senses.whyCN: 科学方法把核算程序化：步骤被安排得可复核，rationally 标记的正是这种秩序。

senses.title: Within legal review
senses.titleCN: 法律上合理关联地：通过合理性审查
senses.definition: in law, describing a rule or classification that has a reasonable connection to a legitimate purpose
senses.definitionCN: 法律上形容规则或分类与合法目的之间具有合理联系
senses.example: A rule must be rationally related to a legitimate public purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 一项规则必须与合法的公共目的具有合理关联。
senses.why: Courts borrowed the word for a low-level test: the question is not whether the policy is wise, but whether the link to its aim can be reasoned.
senses.whyCN: 法院借用该词作为低强度审查标准：问题不是政策是否明智，而是它与目标之间的联系能否被推理支持。

senses.title: For defensible reasons
senses.titleCN: 有可辩护理由地：行动者能说明缘由
senses.definition: in philosophy of action, acting for reasons that the agent could state and defend
senses.definitionCN: 在行动哲学中，指行为者能陈述并辩护其理由地行动
senses.example: An agent acts rationally when it has reasons it can defend to others.
senses.exampleCN: 当行动者拥有能向他人辩护的理由时，它便是在理性地行动。
senses.why: This sense ties the adverb to accountability: not merely efficient, but answerable, as if giving a reckoning.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把副词与可交代性联系起来：不只是高效，还要能作答，仿佛要交出账目。

senses.title: Calmly
senses.titleCN: 冷静地：不让情绪主导
senses.definition: in a calm, controlled way that is not driven by emotion
senses.definitionCN: 以平静克制、不受情绪驱动的方式
senses.example: He responded rationally even when the audience provoked him.
senses.exampleCN: 即使观众激他，他仍理性回应。
senses.why: Emotion and reason are habitually opposed, so doing something rationally came to mean doing it without a heated rush.
senses.whyCN: 情绪与理性常被视为对立，因此「理性地做某事」逐渐也指不带情绪冲动地做。

senses.title: Efficiently toward a goal
senses.titleCN: 工具性地：只按目标效率计算
senses.definition: in a way that calculates the most efficient means to a chosen end
senses.definitionCN: 以计算达成既定目标的最有效手段的方式
senses.example: The plan was rationally efficient but aimed at the wrong goal.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划在工具意义上很高效，却指向了错误的目标。
senses.why: When means are separated from ends, rationally narrows to instrumental calculation: the adverb praises the route without judging the destination.
senses.whyCN: 当手段与目的分离，rationally 就收窄为工具性计算：副词称赞路线，却不评判目的地。

intro.en: Rationally is rational plus the adverb ending -ly, whose Old English ancestor -lice marked manner. The base adjective comes from Latin rationalis.
intro.cn: rationally 是 rational 加副词词尾 -ly，其古英语前身 -lice 标记方式。词基形容词出自拉丁 rationalis。

items.en: Latin ratio 'reckoning, account, reason' is the source of the whole family; it comes from ratus, past participle of reri 'to reckon'.
items.cn: 拉丁 ratio「计算、账目、理性」是整个词族的源头；它出自 reri「计算」的过去分词 ratus。

items.en: The adjective rationalis meant 'belonging to reason, reasonable' and passed into English as rational.
items.cn: 形容词 rationalis 意为「属于理性的、合理的」，进入英语作 rational。

items.en: The Old English suffix -lice, later -ly, turned adjectives into adverbs of manner. English already used this pattern freely when rational arrived.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -lice（后为 -ly）把形容词变为方式副词。rational 进入英语时，这一构词模式已可自由使用。

items.en: Rationally is an English internal formation rather than a direct Latin borrowing; its first recorded uses are early modern.
items.cn: rationally 是英语内部构成，而非直接借自拉丁；最早记录见于近代早期。

items.en: Law, economics and philosophy each fixed the adverb in set phrases such as rationally related and rationally allocate.
items.cn: 法学、经济学与哲学各自把该副词固定进短语，如「具有合理关联」「合理配置」。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of Latin reri is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑，拉丁 reri 的更深来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group separates words of the ratio family that differ in part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms for manner.
note.cn: 第一组区分 ratio 词族中词性不同的词；第二组给出表示方式的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a person, act or argument; rationally is the adverb describing how the act is done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述人、行为或论证；rationally 是副词，描述行为如何完成。

entries.definition: The quality itself. You can praise rationality, but you act rationally.
entries.definitionCN: 指性质本身：可以称赞 rationality，但行动时用 rationally。

entries.definition: The set of reasons behind a decision; it is a thing you give, not a way you act.
entries.definitionCN: 指决策背后的理由体系；是给出的东西，不是行动方式。

entries.definition: This word itself; it answers 'how?' rather than 'what?'
entries.definitionCN: 本词；回答「怎样」而非「什么」。

entries.definition: In a way that follows formal inference. Rationally is broader: it can include judgment and evidence, not only deduction.
entries.definitionCN: 以符合形式推理的方式。rationally 范围更广，可包含判断与证据，不只演绎。

entries.definition: In a way that shows good practical judgment. It stresses prudence more than logical structure.
entries.definitionCN: 以显示良好实践判断的方式，更强调审慎而非逻辑结构。

entries.definition: In a fair, moderate way. In law it often sets a standard of fairness, not of calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 以公平、适度的方式；法律中常设公平标准，而非计算标准。

entries.definition: Without emotional disturbance. Calmly describes the temper; rationally describes the basis of the decision.
entries.definitionCN: 不带情绪波动。calmly 描述性情，rationally 描述决策依据。

entries.definition: After careful consideration, or sometimes intentionally. It stresses the pause before acting rather than the logic used.
entries.definitionCN: 经过仔细考虑，或有时指故意；强调行动前的停顿，而非所用的逻辑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: rational + -ly: doing something in the manner of ratio, by reckoning.
normal.cn: rational + -ly：以 ratio 的方式、靠核算来做某事。

normal.en: The family runs rational, rationality, rationale, rationalize, irrational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rational、rationality、rationale、rationalize、irrational。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: think rationally, act rationally, respond rationally, rationally related to.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示范围：理性思考、理性行动、理性回应、具有合理关联。

normal.en: Legal use is a low-level test: only a reasonable link is required.
normal.cn: 法律用法是低强度审查：只要求存在合理联系。

normal.en: Rationality is the noun; rationally is how the verb is done.
normal.cn: rationality 是名词；rationally 说明动词怎样完成。

abstract.en: Picture two columns of figures being compared line by line before a decision.
abstract.cn: 想象决策前把两列数字逐行比对。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing aside a loud red button and reaching for the written procedure.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手推开醒目的红色按钮，转而拿起书面程序。

abstract.en: Picture a route-finder that draws the shortest path but leaves the destination blank.
abstract.cn: 想象路线规划器画出最短路径，却把目的地留空。

examples.en: Even under pressure, the pilot acted rationally and ran the checklist.
examples.cn: 即使在压力下，飞行员仍理性行动，执行了检查单。

examples.en: The city rationally allocated its water budget among competing districts.
examples.cn: 该市在相互竞争的各区之间合理分配了水预算。

examples.en: A law that treats two similar groups differently must be rationally related to a valid aim.
examples.cn: 对两个相似群体区别对待的法律，必须与正当目标具有合理关联。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rational（理性的）+ ly」——按账目算清楚再做 → rationally 理性地

root: 拉丁 ratio「计算、理性」→ rationalis「合理的」→ 英语 rational + -ly（方式副词词尾）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show the same adverb applied at different scales: a mind weighing evidence, a household choosing sensibly, an economy allocating, a court reviewing, an agent answering for its reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展示同一个副词在不同尺度上的用法：心智权衡证据、家庭明智选择、经济配置资源、法院进行审查、行动者为自己的理由作答。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two columns of figures compared line by line before a nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：两列数字逐行比对后才点头。

branches.en: EVERYDAY REASON: weigh evidence, then choose what common sense endorses.
branches.cn: 日常理性：权衡证据，再选择常识认可的做法。

branches.en: ECONOMIC CALCULATION: cost and benefit decide the allocation.
branches.cn: 经济核算：成本与收益决定配置。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND LAW: order the steps, or show a reasonable link to a legitimate aim.
branches.cn: 程序与法律：安排步骤，或证明与合法目标有合理联系。

branches.en: ACCOUNTABILITY AND TEMPER: reasons must be defensible, and emotion must not drive the act.
branches.cn: 可交代与性情：理由须可辩护，情绪不得主导行为。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTAL EDGE: the most efficient route can still serve an unexamined goal.
branches.cn: 工具性边缘：最高效的路线仍可能服务于未经审视的目标。

intro.en: Rationally is a layered English word: a Latin adjective, an English adjective suffix history, and the native adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: rationally 是分层构成的英语词：拉丁形容词，经由英语形容词形态，再加本族副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The ratio family runs ratio, rational, rationality, rationale, rationalize, ration and rate; all keep the core idea of counting and accounting.
latinIntro.cn: ratio 词族包括 ratio、rational、rationality、rationale、rationalize、ration、rate，都保留计数与核算的核心义。

items.example: The board rationally rejected the riskiest option.
items.exampleCN: 董事会理性地否决了风险最高的选项。

items.example: A rational plan states its assumptions.
items.exampleCN: 理性的计划会说明其假设。

items.example: The paper defends the rationality of the rule.
items.exampleCN: 论文为该规则的合理性辩护。

items.example: They rationalized the workflow to cut delays.
items.exampleCN: 他们重整流程以减少延误。

items.example: The memo sets out the rationale for the merger.
items.exampleCN: 备忘录说明了合并的理由。

items.example: The ration was cut to half a loaf a day.
items.exampleCN: 配给减到每天半条面包。

items.example: The birth rate fell for a third year.
items.exampleCN: 出生率连续第三年下降。

items.meaning: in a way contrary to reason
items.example: He irrationally blamed the weather for his loss.
items.exampleCN: 他非理性地把损失归咎于天气。

definition_zh: 重建；重建物；复原；（语言学）构拟；重建时期
definition_en: the act or result of building something again, or of piecing together something that is no longer intact
core_image: 散落一地的碎石被按编号重新拼回一座拱门
scene: The reconstruction of the bridge took three years and twice the original budget.
sceneCN: 这里 reconstruction 指「实体重建」（第 1 个义项：把被毁的结构重新建起）；句意：这座桥的重建用了三年，花费是最初预算的两倍。图中可辨识物件：编号石块、拱门、吊车、图纸。

pos.zh: 重建；重建物；复原；（语言学）构拟；（美国史）重建时期（作专有名词时大写）

forms.label: 专有名词
forms.form: the Reconstruction（美国重建时期，首字母大写）

senses.title: Rebuilding a damaged structure
senses.titleCN: 实体重建：把被毁的建筑重新建起
senses.definition: the act of building again something that was destroyed or badly damaged
senses.definitionCN: 把被摧毁或严重损坏的事物重新建造起来的行动
senses.example: The reconstruction of the bridge took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的重建用了三年。
senses.why: The noun joins re- 'again' to construction, from Latin construere 'to pile up together', so it means piling the same structure up once more.
senses.whyCN: 该名词把 re-「再次」与 construction 结合，后者出自拉丁 construere「堆叠在一起」，因此意为把同一结构再堆起来一次。

senses.title: Recreating a past event
senses.titleCN: 事件还原：根据线索复原经过
senses.definition: the act of piecing together what happened from remaining evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据残存证据把发生过的事情拼合出来
senses.example: Police reconstructed the accident from skid marks and camera footage.
senses.exampleCN: 警方根据刹车痕与监控画面还原了事故经过。
senses.why: The image shifts from stone to evidence: what is rebuilt is no longer a wall but a sequence of events.
senses.whyCN: 意象从石头转向证据：被重建的不再是一堵墙，而是一连串事件。

senses.title: Linguistic reconstruction
senses.titleCN: 语言构拟：由现存语言反推古语形式
senses.definition: in linguistics, the inferred recovery of an earlier language form from its surviving descendants
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中，从现存后代语言反推更早语言形式的做法
senses.example: The reconstruction of Proto-Indo-European rests on systematic sound correspondences.
senses.exampleCN: 原始印欧语的构拟依赖系统的语音对应关系。
senses.why: Linguists reconstruct a lost language the way engineers rebuild a bridge: from fragments, but with rules that constrain the guess.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家构拟已消失的语言，如同工程师重建桥梁：从残片出发，但用规则约束猜测。

senses.title: National rebuilding after war
senses.titleCN: 战后国家重建：修复社会与经济
senses.definition: the large-scale rebuilding of a country's buildings, economy and institutions after war or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 战争或灾难后对一个国家建筑、经济与制度的大规模重建
senses.example: Post-war reconstruction reshaped both the city and its politics.
senses.exampleCN: 战后重建同时重塑了这座城市及其政治。
senses.why: The building metaphor scales up: a nation is treated as a structure whose parts must be raised again together.
senses.whyCN: 建筑隐喻被放大：国家被当成一座结构，其各部分必须再次一起立起。

senses.title: Surgical reconstruction
senses.titleCN: 手术重建：修复身体结构
senses.definition: in medicine, surgery that rebuilds a body part damaged by injury, disease or congenital condition
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指重建因伤、病或先天状况受损的身体部位的手术
senses.example: Reconstruction of her jaw followed the removal of the tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 切除肿瘤之后，她接受了下颌重建手术。
senses.why: Medicine applies the word to flesh: the damaged part is rebuilt rather than merely repaired at the surface.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个词用于身体：受损部位是被重建，而不只是表面修补。

senses.title: Image and signal reconstruction
senses.titleCN: 图像重建：由探测数据还原画面
senses.definition: in imaging and signal processing, the computation that turns raw detector measurements into a readable image
senses.definitionCN: 在成像与信号处理中，把探测器原始测量换算成可读图像的计算过程
senses.example: Image reconstruction turns detector signals into a readable CT scan.
senses.exampleCN: 图像重建把探测器信号变成可读的 CT 扫描图。
senses.why: Here reconstruction is mathematical: the object is not physically rebuilt, only recovered from data.
senses.whyCN: 这里的重建是数学性的：物体并未被物理重建，只是从数据中被还原出来。

senses.title: Memory reconstruction
senses.titleCN: 记忆重构：回忆是对过去的再拼装
senses.definition: in psychology, the view that remembering is an active rebuilding of past experience rather than a faithful replay
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中认为记忆是对过去经验的主动重建，而非忠实回放的观点
senses.example: Memory is partly a reconstruction, not a faithful recording.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆在某种程度上是重构，而不是忠实录音。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the building metaphor for the mind: recall selects and reassembles fragments, and the result may differ from the original.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把建筑隐喻借给心智：回忆挑选并重新拼合碎片，其结果可能与原初不同。

senses.title: The American Reconstruction era
senses.titleCN: 美国重建时期：南北战争后的政治阶段
senses.definition: in United States history, the period after the Civil War when the Union rebuilt the South's politics and society
senses.definitionCN: 美国历史中指南北战争后联邦重建南方政治与社会的时期
senses.example: The Reconstruction era left a long mark on voting rights.
senses.exampleCN: 重建时期在投票权问题上留下了长久印记。
senses.why: The proper noun applies the general word to a whole national project, and the capital R marks it as a named historical period.
senses.whyCN: 这个专有名词把一般词用于一项全国工程，大写 R 标明它是有名称的历史时期。

intro.en: Reconstruction is re- plus construction, and construction comes from Latin construere 'to pile up, build'. The word is an English formation on Latin materials rather than a direct Latin borrowing.
intro.cn: reconstruction 是 re- 加 construction，而 construction 出自拉丁 construere「堆积、建造」。该词是用拉丁材料在英语中构成的，并非直接借自拉丁。

items.en: Latin struere meant 'to pile up, build, arrange'. Its compounds include construere 'to build together' and destructure 'to tear down'.
items.cn: 拉丁 struere 意为「堆积、建造、安排」，其复合词包括 construere「一起建造」与 destructure「拆毁」。

items.en: Construere joined com- 'together' to struere, giving the image of materials piled into one structure; English construct comes from it.
items.cn: construere 把 com-「一起」加到 struere 上，形成「材料堆成一个结构」的意象；英语 construct 由此而来。

items.en: The prefix re- means 'again' or 'back'. Added to construction, it marks a second building of what already existed or was destroyed.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 意为「再次」或「回」。加到 construction 上，它标记对已存在或被毁之物进行第二次建造。

items.en: Reconstruction appears in English by the late eighteenth century; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: reconstruction 于 18 世纪晚期出现在英语中；最早确切书证存疑。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries extended it to linguistic reconstruction, memory reconstruction and computed image reconstruction.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把它扩展到语言构拟、记忆重构与计算图像重建。

items.en: The precise date of first English use and the earliest sense (physical rebuilding or figurative recovery) are uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与最早义项）：英语首用确切年代以及最早义项（实体重建还是比喻性复原）均存疑。

note.en: The first group separates parts of the construct family; the second gives near-synonyms that stress restoring, recreating or remaking.
note.cn: 第一组区分 construct 词族的不同形式；第二组给出强调修复、再现或重制的近义词。

entries.definition: The original act of building. Reconstruction adds the idea of a second time after damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指最初的建造行为。reconstruction 增加了「受损后再来一次」的意思。

entries.definition: The verb 'to build', or a noun for an idea assembled from parts. It does not imply rebuilding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「建造」，或指由部分拼合的观念；不含「重建」义。

entries.definition: To build again or piece together; reconstruction is the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 指重建或拼合；reconstruction 是动作或其结果。

entries.definition: Describing surgery or work that rebuilds a part; it modifies a noun rather than naming the process.
entries.definitionCN: 形容重建某部位的手术或工作；修饰名词，不命名过程本身。

entries.definition: Bringing something back to a former condition, often with fidelity to the original. Reconstruction may use new materials.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物恢复到从前的状态，常强调忠于原貌；reconstruction 可以使用新材料。

entries.definition: The everyday word for building again. It is narrower and rarely used for ideas or data.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用语，指再次建造；范围较窄，很少用于观念或数据。

entries.definition: Can mean the act of creating again, but usually means leisure activity. Context decides, and it is not a synonym for reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 可指再次创造，但通常指休闲活动；由语境决定，并非 reconstruction 的同义词。

entries.definition: The process of getting something back or returning to health. It stresses the return, not the rebuilding work.
entries.definitionCN: 指取回某物或恢复健康的过程，强调「回来」，而非重建工作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + construct 'pile up' + -ion: piling the same structure up again.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ construct「堆起」+ -ion：把同一结构再堆一次。

normal.en: The family runs construct, construction, reconstruct, reconstructive, structure.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 construct、construction、reconstruct、reconstructive、structure。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: post-war reconstruction, linguistic reconstruction, image reconstruction, memory reconstruction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：战后重建、语言构拟、图像重建、记忆重构。

normal.en: A reconstruction can be physical, evidentiary, linguistic, surgical or computational.
normal.cn: 重建可以是实体的、证据性的、语言的、手术的或计算的。

normal.en: The capital-R Reconstruction names a US historical period, not any ordinary rebuilding.
normal.cn: 大写 Reconstruction 指美国一个历史时期，而非任何普通重建。

abstract.en: Picture numbered fragments of an arch laid out on the floor, waiting to be fitted back together.
abstract.cn: 想象拱门的编号碎片摊在地上，等待被重新拼合。

abstract.en: Picture a detective arranging photographs on a board until the order of events appears.
abstract.cn: 想象侦探在板上排列照片，直到事件顺序浮现。

abstract.en: Picture a scanner circling a body and a computer drawing the inside from echoes.
abstract.cn: 想象扫描仪绕着人体旋转，计算机据回声画出内部。

examples.en: The reconstruction of the cathedral used stone from the original quarry.
examples.cn: 大教堂的重建使用了原采石场的石料。

examples.en: Historians' reconstruction of the battle depends on letters from both sides.
examples.cn: 历史学家对这场战役的还原依赖双方的来信。

examples.en: Memory reconstruction can add details that were never present.
examples.cn: 记忆重构可能加入从未存在过的细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ construction（建造）」——再建一遍 → reconstruction 重建、复原

root: 拉丁 struere「堆积、建造」→ construere「一起建造」→ 英语 construct / construction；加 re-「再次」与 -ion 构成 reconstruction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rebuild different things: a bridge, an event, a lost language, a nation, a body, an image, a memory, and a historical era.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项重建的对象各不相同：一座桥、一起事件、一门失传语言、一个国家、一具身体、一幅图像、一段记忆，以及一个历史时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered fragments of an arch fitted back into one structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：带编号的拱门碎片被重新拼成一个结构。

branches.en: STONE AND EVENTS: either a physical structure or a sequence of happenings is put back together.
branches.cn: 石头与事件：或是一个实体结构，或是一串发生之事被重新拼合。

branches.en: LOST LANGUAGE: fragments of descendants constrain the inferred ancestor.
branches.cn: 失传语言：后代语言的碎片约束对祖语的推断。

branches.en: NATION: a whole society is rebuilt, whether as a general project or a named era.
branches.cn: 国家：整个社会被重建，或作为一般工程，或作为有名称的时代。

branches.en: BODY: surgery rebuilds a damaged part rather than merely patching its surface.
branches.cn: 身体：手术重建受损部位，而不只是修补表面。

branches.en: DATA AND MIND: computation or recall reassembles a whole from fragments, without physical rebuilding.
branches.cn: 数据与心智：计算或回忆由碎片重组整体，并无物理重建。

intro.en: Reconstruction stacks three layers: the Latin verb struere 'pile up', the English noun construction, and the prefix re- 'again' plus -ion.
intro.cn: reconstruction 叠了三层：拉丁动词 struere「堆积」、英语名词 construction，再加前缀 re-「再次」与 -ion。

latinIntro.en: The struere family includes structure, construct, construction, destruct, instruct, obstruct and instrument, all built on the image of piling or arranging materials.
latinIntro.cn: struere 词族包括 structure、construct、construction、destruct、instruct、obstruct、instrument，都建立在堆积或安排材料的意象上。

items.meaning: the act or result of building again
items.example: The reconstruction of the school finished ahead of schedule.
items.exampleCN: 学校的重建提前完成。

items.meaning: to build again or piece together
items.example: Engineers reconstructed the failed joint in a test rig.
items.exampleCN: 工程师在试验台上重建了失效的接点。

items.meaning: the act of building; a structure
items.example: Construction of the tunnel began in spring.
items.exampleCN: 隧道的建造在春季开始。

items.example: They constructed a model from cardboard.
items.exampleCN: 他们用纸板搭了一个模型。

items.meaning: an arranged whole; the arrangement itself
items.example: The structure survived the flood.
items.exampleCN: 该结构在洪水中幸存。

items.meaning: to build knowledge into someone; to teach
items.meaningCN: 把知识建构进某人；教导
items.example: The manual instructs users to oil the hinge.
items.exampleCN: 手册指导用户给铰链上油。

items.meaning: to build in the way; to block
items.example: Fallen trees obstructed the road.
items.exampleCN: 倒下的树阻塞了道路。

items.example: The command destructs the old archive.
items.exampleCN: 该命令会销毁旧档案。

definition_zh: 娱乐的；休闲的；消遣性的；非医疗用途的
definition_en: relating to leisure activities done for pleasure, or describing a use that is not the officially intended or medical one
core_image: 湖面上一条小船、一只钓竿和一把折叠椅，旁边立着「休闲区」木牌
scene: The lake's recreational use is limited to boating, fishing and swimming.
sceneCN: 这里 recreational 指「休闲用途的」（第 8 个义项：水域被用于消遣而非工业或供水）；句意：该湖的休闲用途限于划船、垂钓与游泳。图中可辨识物件：小船、钓竿、折叠椅、休闲区木牌。

pos.zh: 娱乐的；休闲的；消遣性的；（药物等）非医疗用途的

forms.label: 动词形式
forms.form: recreate（娱乐；消遣；另注意 re-create 意为「重新创造」）

derivatives.zh: 娱乐；消遣（与 re-create「重新创造」拼写相同、来源不同）
恢复精神的；消遣的（少用）

senses.title: Relating to leisure
senses.titleCN: 休闲的：为消遣而非工作而设
senses.definition: connected with activities people do for enjoyment when they are not working
senses.definitionCN: 与人们不工作时为享乐而做的活动有关
senses.example: The town built a recreational complex beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇在河边建了一座休闲综合体。
senses.why: Recreation comes from Latin recreare 'to restore to health'; the adjective marks whatever serves that restoring purpose.
senses.whyCN: recreation 出自拉丁 recreare「使恢复健康」；形容词标记的是服务于这种恢复作用的事物。

senses.title: Of facilities and land
senses.titleCN: 休闲设施的：指场地与设备的规划用途
senses.definition: describing land, buildings or equipment planned for leisure rather than production
senses.definitionCN: 形容为休闲而非生产而规划的场地、建筑或设备
senses.example: The recreational area includes courts, a pool and a picnic lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 休闲区包括球场、泳池和野餐草坪。
senses.why: Planning law needs a label for land set aside for play, and recreational fills that slot in zoning maps.
senses.whyCN: 规划法规需要给留作游憩的土地一个标签，recreational 正好填补分区图上的这一位置。

senses.title: Non-medical drug use
senses.titleCN: 娱乐性用药：非医疗目的的药物使用
senses.definition: describing the use of a drug for pleasure rather than medical treatment, often with a cautionary tone
senses.definitionCN: 形容出于享乐而非治疗目的使用药物，常带警示语气
senses.example: Recreational drug use can still cause serious harm.
senses.exampleCN: 娱乐性药物使用仍可能造成严重伤害。
senses.why: The adjective separates pleasure from prescription: the same substance is medical in a clinic and recreational at a party.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把享乐与处方分开：同一种物质在诊所是医疗用途，在聚会上则是娱乐用途。

senses.title: Fishing or hunting for pleasure
senses.titleCN: 休闲渔猎：以消遣为目的的捕捞
senses.definition: describing fishing, hunting or gathering done mainly for enjoyment, usually under specific rules
senses.definitionCN: 形容主要以消遣为目的的捕鱼、打猎或采集，通常受特定规则约束
senses.example: Recreational fishing requires a licence and daily catch limits.
senses.exampleCN: 休闲垂钓需要许可证，并有每日捕捞限额。
senses.why: Resource managers distinguish use for livelihood from use for pleasure, and the adjective marks the second.
senses.whyCN: 资源管理者把生计性利用与消遣性利用分开，这个形容词标记后者。

senses.title: Recreational vehicle
senses.titleCN: 休闲车的：房车一类移动住宿工具
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase recreational vehicle, a large vehicle used for travel and camping
senses.definitionCN: 在固定短语 recreational vehicle 中，指用于旅行与露营的大型车辆
senses.example: They spent the summer in a recreational vehicle along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个夏天开着房车沿海岸旅行。
senses.why: The phrase names a vehicle whose purpose is leisure, so the adjective replaces a longer description of use.
senses.whyCN: 该短语命名一种以休闲为目的的车辆，形容词替代了更长的用途描述。

senses.title: Mathematics for enjoyment
senses.titleCN: 趣味数学：以游戏心态研究数学
senses.definition: describing puzzles, games and problems studied for delight rather than application
senses.definitionCN: 形容为乐趣而非应用而研究的谜题、游戏与问题
senses.example: Recreational mathematics includes Sudoku and magic squares.
senses.exampleCN: 趣味数学包括数独与幻方。
senses.why: The label borrows the leisure sense and applies it to an intellectual hobby, marking work done for fun.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签借用了休闲义，用于智力爱好，标记「为乐趣而做」的工作。

senses.title: Reading for pleasure
senses.titleCN: 消遣性阅读：不为任务而读
senses.definition: describing reading chosen for enjoyment rather than study or duty
senses.definitionCN: 形容为享受而非学习或任务而选择的阅读
senses.example: She keeps a stack of recreational reading beside her desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她桌边放着一摞消遣读物。
senses.why: Educators contrast required reading with reading done for pleasure, and recreational names the latter.
senses.whyCN: 教育者把必读书目与为乐趣而读的书区分开，recreational 命名后者。

senses.title: Leisure use of a resource
senses.titleCN: 资源的休闲用途：水域或土地的非生产使用
senses.definition: describing the use of water, land or a resource for leisure rather than industry or supply
senses.definitionCN: 形容水域、土地或资源被用于休闲，而非工业或供给
senses.example: The reservoir balances recreational use against drinking water needs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座水库要在休闲用途与饮用水需求之间取得平衡。
senses.why: Management must name every competing use; recreational is the label for swimming, boating and angling.
senses.whyCN: 管理必须为每一种相互竞争的用途命名；recreational 是游泳、划船与垂钓的标签。

intro.en: Recreational is an English adjective built on recreation, which comes from Latin recreare 'to restore'. Its resemblance to re-creation 'creating again' is a coincidence of spelling, not of origin.
intro.cn: recreational 是建立在 recreation 之上的英语形容词，后者出自拉丁 recreare「使恢复」。它与 re-creation「重新创造」的相似只是拼写巧合，并非同源。

items.en: Latin creare meant 'to bring forth, produce, create'. Its family includes create, creature, creation and creator.
items.cn: 拉丁 creare 意为「产生、制造、创造」，其词族包括 create、creature、creation、creator。

items.en: Recreare added re- 'again' to creare, but the sense was 'to restore, refresh, revive', especially after effort or illness — not 'to create again'.
items.cn: recreare 在 creare 上加 re-「再次」，但词义是「恢复、提神、复苏」，尤指劳累或患病之后，而非「再次创造」。

items.en: The Latin noun recreatio named refreshment or recovery. Old French recreation carried it into English in the fourteenth century as 'refreshment of body or mind'.
items.cn: 拉丁名词 recreatio 指「恢复精神、休养」。古法语 recreation 于 14 世纪把它带入英语，意为「身心恢复」。

items.en: By the sixteenth century recreation meant pleasurable activity that refreshes, and the modern leisure sense dominated.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，recreation 指能恢复精神的愉悦活动，现代「休闲」义逐渐占主导。

items.en: Recreational appears later, formed in English with -al, and spreads into land planning, medicine, transport and mathematics.
items.cn: recreational 出现更晚，由英语加 -al 构成，并扩散到土地规划、医学、交通与数学领域。

items.en: The exact first English date of recreational is uncertain, and the homograph re-creation is a separate formation that happens to share spelling.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：recreational 英语首见确切年代存疑；同形词 re-creation 是另一条构词路径，只是拼写相同。

note.en: The first group separates the recreation family, including the misleading homograph; the second gives near-synonyms for leisure and pleasure.
note.cn: 第一组区分 recreation 词族，包括那个容易误导的同形词；第二组给出与休闲、享乐相关的近义词。

entries.definition: The activity itself, or the refreshment it brings; recreational is the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指休闲活动本身或其恢复作用；recreational 是放在名词前的形容词。

entries.definition: Written with a hyphen, it means to make something anew. It is not related to recreation in the leisure sense.
entries.definitionCN: 带连字符时意为「重新创造」，与休闲义的 recreation 不同源。

entries.definition: An uncommon synonym for refreshing or recreational; modern usage prefers recreational.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的同义形容词，意为「提神的」或「休闲的」；现代多用 recreational。

entries.definition: A rare noun for someone who takes part in recreation; it cannot modify a facility.
entries.definitionCN: 少见的「休闲活动参与者」名词，不能用来修饰设施。

entries.definition: Time free from work. Leisure is the time; recreational describes what fills it.
entries.definitionCN: 指不工作的时间。leisure 是时间，recreational 描述用来填满时间的内容。

entries.definition: An activity done for enjoyment. It is a countable noun, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指为享乐而做的活动；是可数名词，不是形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being entertained, or an entertaining thing. It stresses fun more than restoration.
entries.definitionCN: 指被逗乐的状态或娱乐事物，更强调趣味而非恢复。

entries.definition: Not used for medical treatment. In drug contexts it overlaps sense 3 but is neutral rather than cautionary.
entries.definitionCN: 指不用于医疗；在药物语境中与第 3 个义项重叠，但语气中性，不带警示。

entries.definition: Relaxed in style or unofficial in status. It does not by itself mean leisure-oriented.
entries.definitionCN: 指风格随和或地位非正式；本身并不表示「以休闲为目的」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: recreare 'restore' + -al: belonging to what restores you after work.
normal.cn: recreare「恢复」+ -al：属于「工作后让你恢复」的事物。

normal.en: The family runs recreate, recreation, recreative, recreationalist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 recreate、recreation、recreative、recreationalist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: recreational facilities, recreational area, recreational vehicle, recreational mathematics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：休闲设施、休闲区、休闲车、趣味数学。

normal.en: re-create with a hyphen means 'create again'; recreation without it usually means leisure.
normal.cn: 带连字符的 re-create 意为「重新创造」；不带连字符的 recreation 通常指休闲。

normal.en: recreational drug use is defined by purpose, not by the substance alone.
normal.cn: 娱乐性用药是按目的界定，而非仅按物质本身界定。

abstract.en: Picture a boat, a fishing rod and a folding chair waiting by a lake at sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象日出时湖边放着一条小船、一根钓竿和一把折叠椅。

abstract.en: Picture a worker leaving a factory gate and immediately sitting down to a game of chess.
abstract.cn: 想象工人走出厂门，立刻坐下下一盘棋。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir with a line drawn across it: drinking water on one side, swimmers on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象水库被一条线分开：一边是饮用水，一边是游泳的人。

examples.en: The city added recreational space instead of another car park.
examples.cn: 这座城市增加了休闲空间，而不是再建一个停车场。

examples.en: The survey asked about recreational water use in the lake district.
examples.cn: 调查询问了湖区水域的休闲用途。

examples.en: Recreational mathematics treats a hard proof as a puzzle to enjoy.
examples.cn: 趣味数学把艰难的证明当作可供享受的谜题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ creation（创造）」——工作后再造精神 → recreational 休闲的、娱乐的

root: 拉丁 creare「创造」→ recreare「恢复、提神」→ recreatio「休养」→ 英语 recreation；加 -al 成 recreational。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses extend one idea: an activity restores the person who does it, and the adjective marks every setting, substance or resource put to that restoring, non-serious purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项扩展一个观念：活动使做它的人恢复，而形容词标记一切为这种恢复性、非严肃目的而设的场所、物质或资源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat, a rod and a folding chair waiting by a lake.
core.cn: 核心意象：湖边等待使用的船、钓竿与折叠椅。

branches.en: LEISURE SETTING: activity and the places planned for it.
branches.cn: 休闲场景：活动本身以及为其规划的场所。

branches.en: PLEASURE WITHOUT PRESCRIPTION: the same substance used for fun, with a warning built in.
branches.cn: 无处方之乐：同一种物质被用于享乐，语气自带警示。

branches.en: RESOURCE USE: fishing, hunting, boating and swimming compete with production and supply.
branches.cn: 资源利用：渔猎、划船与游泳同生产及供给争夺同一资源。

branches.en: THE VEHICLE: a machine whose whole purpose is leisure travel.
branches.cn: 交通工具：整台机器的用途就是休闲旅行。

branches.en: PLAY WITH IDEAS: puzzles and pleasure reading apply leisure to the mind.
branches.cn: 与观念游戏：谜题与消遣阅读把休闲用于心智。

intro.en: Recreational is a Latin verb of restoration turned into an English noun and then an adjective: recreare, recreatio, recreation, recreational.
intro.cn: recreational 由表示恢复的拉丁动词转为英语名词、再转为形容词：recreare、recreatio、recreation、recreational。

latinIntro.en: The creare family includes create, creative, creation, creature and recreation; note that re-creation 'creating again' is a different formation with the same spelling.
latinIntro.cn: creare 词族包括 create、creative、creation、creature、recreation；注意 re-creation「重新创造」是同形拼写但不同来源的构词。

items.example: The recreational budget rose by ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 休闲预算增加了百分之十。

items.example: Recreation is protected in the zoning plan.
items.exampleCN: 分区规划保护休闲用地。

items.meaning: to refresh oneself; to take recreation
items.example: The family recreates at the lake each summer.
items.exampleCN: 这家人每年夏天在湖边消遣。

items.example: A recreative walk cleared his mind.
items.exampleCN: 一次提神的散步使他头脑清明。

items.example: The team created a new game.
items.exampleCN: 团队创造了一个新游戏。

items.meaning: the act or product of making
items.example: The mural was a year's creation.
items.exampleCN: 这幅壁画用了一年才创作完成。

items.example: She found a creative solution.
items.exampleCN: 她找到了一个有创意的解决方案。

items.example: The cave holds rare creatures.
items.exampleCN: 洞里有稀有生物。

definition_zh: 减少；削减；降低；还原；（数学）约简；（烹饪）收汁
definition_en: the act of making something smaller or simpler, or the amount by which it is made smaller
core_image: 一块厚布被两边慢慢拉紧，最后缩成一小片
scene: The new boiler led to a twenty percent reduction in fuel use.
sceneCN: 这里 reduction 指「用量下降的幅度」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度变小）；句意：新锅炉使燃料用量减少了百分之二十。图中可辨识物件：旧锅炉、新锅炉、下降箭头、用量表。

pos.zh: 减少；削减；降低；（化学）还原；（数学）约简；（烹饪）收汁

collocations.zh: 归谬法（reductio ad absurdum 的英语说法）

forms.label: 可数性说明
forms.form: reduction（指动作或过程时多不可数，指一次削减时可数）

senses.title: A decrease in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量减少：总量或程度变小
senses.definition: the act or result of making an amount, rate or level smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使数量、比率或水平变小的动作或结果
senses.example: The new boiler led to a twenty percent reduction in fuel use.
senses.exampleCN: 新锅炉使燃料用量减少了百分之二十。
senses.why: Reduction comes from Latin reducere 'to lead back'; the modern 'make smaller' sense grew from leading something down to a lower level.
senses.whyCN: reduction 出自拉丁 reducere「带回」；现代「使变小」义由「把某物带到更低水平」发展而来。

senses.title: A price cut
senses.titleCN: 降价：售价被调低
senses.definition: a lowering of price, often offered as a discount
senses.definitionCN: 价格的调低，常作为折扣给出
senses.example: The store advertised a fifty-dollar reduction on the jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 商店宣传这件夹克降价五十美元。
senses.why: Commerce applies the physical image of lowering to money: the price is brought down, and the amount is called a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 商业把「降低」的物理意象用于金钱：价格被带下来，降下的数额就叫 reduction。

senses.title: Chemical reduction
senses.titleCN: 化学还原：物质得到电子
senses.definition: in chemistry, the process in which a substance gains electrons and its oxidation state falls
senses.definitionCN: 化学中物质获得电子、氧化态降低的过程
senses.example: Iron ore is turned into metal by chemical reduction in a furnace.
senses.exampleCN: 铁矿石在炉中经化学还原变成金属。
senses.why: Chemists kept the 'lowering' idea: the oxidation number is brought down as electrons are added, so the reaction is a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 化学家保留了「降低」的观念：加入电子后氧化数被带低，因此该反应称为还原。

senses.title: Mathematical simplification
senses.titleCN: 数学约简：把式子化到更简形式
senses.definition: in mathematics, the rewriting of an expression or problem into a simpler equivalent form
senses.definitionCN: 数学中把表达式或问题改写为更简单的等价形式
senses.example: Reduction of the fraction 18/24 gives 3/4.
senses.exampleCN: 把分数 18/24 约简得到 3/4。
senses.why: The 'lead back' sense survives here: a complex expression is led back to its simplest equivalent.
senses.whyCN: 「带回」义在此留存：复杂表达式被带回其最简单的等价形式。

senses.title: Cooking down a sauce
senses.titleCN: 烹煮收汁：水分蒸发使汤汁变浓
senses.definition: in cooking, the evaporation of liquid so that a sauce becomes thicker and more concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 烹饪中液体蒸发、使酱汁变稠变浓的过程
senses.example: A slow reduction concentrates the flavour of the stock.
senses.exampleCN: 慢火收汁使高汤的味道更浓缩。
senses.why: The kitchen borrows the volume sense literally: the liquid is reduced in quantity while the flavour remains.
senses.whyCN: 厨房直接借用了体积义：液体数量变少，而风味保留。

senses.title: Lowering in rank
senses.titleCN: 降级：职位或地位被调低
senses.definition: the act of moving someone to a lower rank, position or status
senses.definitionCN: 把某人调到更低职级、职位或地位的行为
senses.example: His reduction from captain to private was announced at roll call.
senses.exampleCN: 点名列队时宣布他从上尉降为列兵。
senses.why: This sense is the oldest direction of ducere: a person is led back down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项最贴近 ducere 的原始方向：人被沿着等级序列带回下方。

senses.title: Data reduction
senses.titleCN: 数据简化：把原始数据压缩成可用摘要
senses.definition: the process of summarizing or simplifying large sets of raw data into usable measures
senses.definitionCN: 把大量原始数据汇总或简化为可用指标的过程
senses.example: Data reduction turned thousands of sensor readings into one daily average.
senses.exampleCN: 数据简化把数千条传感器读数变成一个日均值。
senses.why: The word is applied to information rather than matter: detail is brought down to a manageable summary.
senses.whyCN: 该词被用于信息而非物质：细节被压到可处理的摘要层级。

senses.title: Reductio ad absurdum
senses.titleCN: 归谬：把命题推到荒谬以反驳它
senses.definition: in logic, the method of disproving a claim by showing that its consequences are absurd
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中通过显示某主张的推论荒谬来反驳它的方法
senses.example: The proof proceeds by reduction to absurdity.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明通过归谬法推进。
senses.why: The Latin phrase reductio ad absurdum means 'a leading back to the absurd': the argument leads the claim back to a contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语 reductio ad absurdum 意为「带回到荒谬」：论证把该主张带回矛盾之处。
